trace.title: Render snapshot
trace.detail:
# The idea

A React render calculates UI from a snapshot of props and state. Event handlers created during that render see that snapshot.

Calling a state setter requests an update; it does not rewrite the local variable in the handler that is already running.

When the next value depends on the previous queued value, use a functional updater. Keep render pure: do not send requests or mutate outside objects while calculating JSX.

Effects synchronize with an external system after a committed render and need cleanup when applicable.

Keys identify sibling items across renders. Stable IDs preserve the right item identity.

Array indexes can attach local row state to the wrong item when the list is reordered. Memoization is a measured performance tool, not a correctness patch.

trace.title: Follow the middle steps
trace.detail:
The updater queue starts with the previous state, then applies +1 three times. The next committed render gets +3.

Direct values computed from one snapshot can instead request the same next value repeatedly.

For an effect subscription: setup attaches to an external source; cleanup detaches before replacement/unmount. Include the values the effect uses.

A missing dependency can keep a handler tied to old values. Development Strict Mode checks can reveal missing cleanup.

trace.title: Check the result
trace.detail:
An effect that only computes fullName from firstName/lastName stores redundant state. Derive it during rendering.

React’s scheduling details do not mean any render is allowed to mutate external state.
